questions.q: How does soluble fiber contribute to lowering blood cholesterol levels?
options: It binds to bile acids in the intestine, promoting their excretion.
It is absorbed into the blood and dissolves cholesterol plaques.
It speeds up the transit time of food, preventing absorption.
It converts cholesterol into glucose in the liver.
questions.explain: Soluble fiber binds with bile acids (made from cholesterol) in the digestive tract, preventing their reabsorption (enterohepatic circulation) and causing the liver to pull more cholesterol from the blood to make new bile.

options: The total amount of carbohydrate in a food.
How much a specific food raises blood glucose compared to a standard (glucose).
The amount of insulin secreted by the pancreas.
questions.explain: Glycemic Index quantifies the blood glucose response to a food containing 50g of available carbohydrates compared to a standard (usually pure glucose).
